Confluent, an IBM company, is pioneering a fundamentally new category of data infrastructure focused on data in motion. Have you ever found a new favorite series on Netflix, picked up groceries curbside at Walmart, or paid for something using Square? That's the power of data in motion in action — giving organizations instant access to the massive amounts of data that is constantly flowing throughout their business. At Confluent, we're building the foundational platform for this new paradigm of data infrastructure.
The Office of the CISO (OCISO) is part of Confluent's Trust and Security organization. Its mission is to earn and retain trust by championing Confluent's security, privacy, resilience, and compliance positions, thereby accelerating customer adoption and use of our platform and products.
OCISO is building a Global Product Regulatory Compliance team: a new function that determines which laws, regulations, and industry frameworks apply to Confluent's products, translates them into product and platform controls, and gives customers, regulators, and our field teams clear and consistent answers. The program covers direct obligations, such as the EU GDPR, Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), and indirect obligations that flow down from customers in financial services, healthcare, the public sector, telecommunications, and other regulated industries. Coverage spans cybersecurity, operational resilience, privacy, sovereignty, AI governance, and third-party risk management.
Confluent operates on a global scale, so you will develop relationships with OCISO team members in the Americas, EMEA, and APAC, and partner closely with IBM's Regulatory Compliance, Legal, and Government & Regulatory Affairs teams. Organizational, interpersonal and communication skills are key to success.
We are looking for a motivated, high energy senior individual contributor who can own and successfully execute with minimal oversight. This is a senior role with real influence and accountability. The right person is able to manage multiple deliverables simultaneously, enjoys doing in-depth regulatory research and analysis, and hands on work, executing deliverables personally, rather than coordinating others. The successful candidate will thrive in ambiguity, is adept at context switching, and comfortable with fluid execution priorities. Heavy AI usage is expected.
Regulatory Compliance Responsibilities
Regulatory Analysis — Review regulatory texts, supervisory guidance, and industry frameworks and best practices. Determine the impact to Confluent's products, and produce clear applicability and impact assessments that state what applies, why, and what it requires of the product. Serve as the subject matter expert on key global regulatory requirements.
Control Posture Assessments — Conduct risk-based posture assessments against priority obligations such as EU DORA and the EU Cyber Resilience Act. Document findings and propose control enhancements or feature build outs to Product or Engineering owners for inclusion in their roadmaps.
Influence Product Strategy — Work directly with Product Managers and Engineering leads to translate regulatory requirements into concrete technical, operational, and product controls. Draft business requirements for product enhancements, and contribute to pre-launch reviews so new products and features meet mandatory controls before general availability.
Regulated Industry & Field Support — Support OCISO customer-facing leads on flow-down obligations from financial services, public sector, and healthcare customers, under frameworks such as SEC Reg SCI, FFIEC, HIPAA, FedRAMP, DORA, NIS2, GDPR, EU AI Act, and the EU Cyber Resilience Act. Turn recurring customer questions into standard, reusable positions.
Audits, Examinations & Incident Notifications — Prepare evidence, documentation, and technical responses for regulatory audits and examinations touching Confluent products (for example, under DORA), coordinated through IBM.
Advisory & Enablement Content — Craft field enablement materials, such as advisory notes for Product regulatory and Engineering, executive summaries, control mappings, FAQs, customer guides, presentations, and training. Contribute to the development of Trust Center content, including white papers and blogs on regulatory trends. Partner with Government & Regulatory Affairs to influence emerging regulations and policies, as needed.
Senior Stakeholder Engagement & Advocacy — Engage as a peer with senior leaders across Confluent Product, Engineering, Trust & Security, GRC, and with IBM Legal, Regulatory Compliance, and Government & Regulatory Affairs.
Privacy Compliance Responsibilities
Privacy compliance program - Operationalize a global privacy compliance program from the ground up. Support new privacy and sovereignty rule implementation, maintain a global rule inventory, map privacy obligations across applicable regimes to documented controls, and complete product PIAs, DPIAs, and IBM’s information governance processes.
Global Privacy SME - Serve as a global privacy expert, providing advisory guidance on privacy rules and regulations, responding to Product questions and assessing new product launches through a privacy control lens.
Influence Product Strategy - Work directly with Product Managers and Engineering leads to translate regulatory requirements into concrete technical, operational, and product controls. Draft business requirements for privacy and sovereignty-related product enhancements, and contribute to pre-launch reviews so new products and features meet mandatory controls before general availability.
Customer notifications - Manage customer cyber incident response notifications in partnership with IBM enterprise teams.
Privacy certifications - Complete and maintain certifications such as the Data Privacy Framework and ISO/IEC 27701.
Advisory & Enablement Content — Craft field enablement materials, such as advisory notes for Product regulatory and Engineering, executive summaries, control mappings, FAQs, customer guides, presentations, and training. Contribute to the development of Trust Center content, including white papers and blogs on regulatory trends. Partner with Government & Regulatory Affairs to influence emerging regulations and policies, as needed.
Senior Stakeholder Engagement & Advocacy — Engage as a peer with senior leaders across Confluent Product, Engineering, Trust & Security, and GRC teams, and with IBM Legal, Compliance, and Government & Regulatory Affairs.
Bachelor's degree and a minimum of 12+ years of experience in regulatory compliance, information security, privacy, or technology risk roles, ideally within a cloud/SaaS provider, a major technology vendor, or a highly regulated enterprise.
Strong issue-spotting judgment: you can read a regulation or supervisory guidance you have not seen before, pinpoint the provisions that matter for a cloud and software platform, and distinguish what can be resolved through control mapping from what needs legal interpretation.
Strong, current knowledge of global frameworks affecting cloud products across cybersecurity, operational resilience, privacy, and AI governance, such as DORA, NIS2, GDPR, the EU AI Act, and the EU Cyber Resilience Act, as well as sector-specific regimes such as those impacting financial services.
Privacy expertise in GDPR, UK GDPR, US state privacy laws, or ISO/IEC 27701, and cross-border transfer mechanisms such as the Data Privacy Framework, and the difference between controller and processor obligations, with particular depth on processors.
Experience with hands-on assessments. You have written DPIAs and PIAs and are technically fluent. You understand data flows, retention, encryption, access controls, and subprocessors well enough to test an engineer’s answer.
Proven experience mapping regulatory requirements to control frameworks (for example, NIST 800-53) and turning them into concrete technical and operational controls with Product and Engineering teams.
A working understanding of cloud-native architecture.
Excellent written and verbal communication. You can write a crisp brief for executives, a precise requirement for engineers, and a defensible regulatory position, and you are comfortable presenting to, and respectfully challenging, senior leaders as a peer.
A track record of hands-on delivery as a senior individual contributor: you personally produce the analyses, mappings, evidence packages, and enablement content, and drive them to completion without a team to delegate to.
Judgment under ambiguity. You can build a program from an ad hoc starting point, and take a practical approach prioritized by risk and market exposure.
Direct experience with financial services regulators and supervisory expectations, such as PRA, FCA, BaFin, OCC, FFIEC, SEC Reg SCI, MAS, APRA, RBI, or SEBI, including outsourcing and ICT third-party risk requirements.
Familiarity with AI/ML security and governance considerations, including evolving regulatory expectations for AI in cloud environments.
Experience with healthcare, public sector, telecommunications, or data sovereignty regimes, such as HIPAA, FedRAMP, the UK Telecommunications (Security) Act, SecNumCloud, or EUCS.
Experience working within or alongside a hyperscaler or large technology vendor, navigating shared or inherited compliance obligations between a parent company and a product line.
Experience using AI tools to accelerate regulatory research, horizon scanning, and control mapping, with the rigor to validate AI-generated output before it reaches customers or regulators.
A law degree.
An IAPP credential such as CIPP/E, CIPP/US, CIPM, or CIPT.

The Senior Manager ensures the team is contributing accurate , relevant and reliable Threats ‘products’ – specifically:
Ensuring both teams ’ focus is set appropriately.
Maintaining overall control of the Threats backlog.
Balancing the need to address short term ‘tactical’ questions with the need to establish practical, appropriate and effective priorities that fulfil IBM’s cyber defense needs.
Collaborating with the TH Manager to set and execute the priorities and direction for the threat hunters.
Ensuring the unique skills and capabilities of all team members are used to best effect.
Ensuring timely collection, processing, analysis and dissemination of intelligence to the right audience. This is vital in ensuring threats are identified quickly and efficiently.
Performing disposition of intelligence to establish its relevance to the corporation – crucially, providing context to all-source intelligence to inform the specific threat to IBM and what mitigation options are available.
The Cyber Security Threats Manager is responsible for building and maintaining the Intelligence collection and dissemination plan - aligned with the ISTAR framework - to support the IBM’s Cyber Defense strategy. A vital part of the Senior Manager’s role is understanding the needs and priority requirements of Threats “ end-users ” – including the other cyber defense teams . Here, the Senior Manager is also part ‘Product Owner’ and is responsible for the developing and maintaining relationships with end-users for mutual benefit. To do this, they must have a sound appreciation of the work performed by other teams and the pressures they face.
Finally, the Senior Manager may also lead work with external agencies – such as ENISA and the NCFTA. At times, this may require them to represent IBM within external communities, which includes conferences and partnership programs.
Deep, demonstrable knowledge of cyber security threats – including attack methods, patterns and practices, adversaries – capabilities, motivations and opportunities, malicious software / living off the land, adversary infrastructure.
Deep knowledge in the decomposition of threats and modeling them to design, implement, tune and manage cyber security defenses.
Thorough, demonstrable understanding of Threat Intelligence practices and tradecraft.
Understanding and practical awareness of Threat Hunting practices and tradecraft, as required to support the Threat Hunt team and set overall direction for the Threats team.
Experience working with external partners including government agencies.
Experience with IBM technologies – hardware and software.
Experience with prototyping and creating early-stage IT infrastructure.
Experience applying AI technologies to reduce toil and in solving practical cyber threats-related problems.
Strong investigative experience.
Experience in software development, security within the development lifecycle and Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery technologies.
Experience working with cyber-physical security teams.
Experience leading and maintaining external partnerships and related programs.
